title: Linux effect conformance
description: Objective: prove provider launch, Git/workspace, locks, signals, cancellation, scope resolution, and crash recovery on supported Linux packaging. Deliverable: Linux effect adapters and fault evidence. NOT in scope: weakening Windows behavior or claiming sandboxing. Hard dependencies: Foundation runner and Codex adapter. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/platform/linux/** and tests/fault/linux/**. Verification: pnpm test:fault.
definitionOfDone: Every declared effect boundary passes crash-before/after activation and cancellation schedules.
Path, symlink, process, lock, and runtime closure observations are proven or UNKNOWN.
Packaging uses the pinned engine/runtime and doctor reports exact versions.
taskRails: Portability consumes frozen daemon/core contracts; adapters cannot fork lifecycle or authority semantics.
Official MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP only; no custom MCP-over-WebSocket dialect.
Unsupported OS/provider/import facts remain typed UNSUPPORTED or UNKNOWN, never guessed.
IDE adapters are thin optional shells for the standalone control room. Keep files below 400 lines and use explicit owned paths.
reopenReason:
Deferred BLOCKED -> BACKLOG by governor-f70d1157 at 14:32Z on human direction. This is a SCOPE DEFERRAL, not a block, and the distinction matters: BLOCKED says "someone should fix this"; BACKLOG-deferred says "this is correctly out of reach until the environment changes".

WHY IT CAN NEVER PASS HERE. Measured: process.platform is win32 x64. DoD 4 requires live Linux process/lock/signal observation. No amount of landed code fixes that — it needs an actual Linux host. Global rail Clause 2 forbids the substitute (off-host fixture-driven schedules certify the fixture, not the platform), and epic rail 4 forbids inventing a pass. So on this machine the task is unsatisfiable by construction, and six architects have now each paid a full context load to re-derive that.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED IN ITS FAVOUR, so this is not written off: packages/runner/src/platform/ NOW EXISTS. task-f01ef545 landed linux-boundary.ts, linux-facts.ts, linux-observation.ts, platform-contract.ts and platform-instant.ts with .js bridges, and published PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES, PLATFORM_LAYERS, PLATFORM_ERROR_CODES, observeLinuxPlatform and classifyLinuxBoundary on the @moe/runner root. That was DoD 1's blocker and it is gone. DoD 2 was always meetable (Linux path/symlink policy is pure logic, permitting typed UNKNOWN by its own wording).

REMAINING, precisely: DoD 3 needs the doctor runtime inventory (task-1cafc7f9, WORKING at 6/7 — nearly landed). DoD 4 needs a Linux host and the test:fault lane (task-b5e9bd64); root package.json still has neither test:fault nor test:security, and tests/fault/ contains only foundation/.

MILESTONE JUSTIFICATION, not just convenience: this task belongs to epic-f02c6977 (M4 Portability). The active epic-bd387eeb is M1 Foundation Preview, whose own description scopes it to "a Windows+Claude single-node vertical slice". Cross-OS conformance is a later milestone by the epic's own definition, so deferring it is consistent with the plan rather than a retreat from it.

DO NOT PROMOTE THIS TO PLANNING on a Windows host. Promote when a Linux host is available AND task-1cafc7f9 and task-b5e9bd64 are DONE. If someone wants the honest half now, the correct move is a NEW narrow task covering DoD 2 only (pure path/symlink policy, typed UNKNOWN elsewhere) — not a re-plan of this one with its DoD quietly narrowed, which Clause 2 forbids.

NOTE ON ORDERING: the human asked for these to sit last. I cannot set `order` — no MCP tool exposes it and hand-editing .moe/tasks JSON while the daemon is live would race other agents. BACKLOG already removes it from the claimable queue, which achieves the operative half.
